Agent Name: Planner  
Step Number: 1  
Reason for Mistake: The Planner made a mistake by stating that acceleration remains constant at 9.8 m/s² downward after the chute opens, which is incorrect in the context of the problem. This error roots in a misunderstanding of the transition of acceleration when the parachute opens. Initially, the acceleration is positive (i.e., in the same direction as velocity, which is downward), but when the chute opens, the acceleration becomes negative relative to the direction of velocity. This results in deceleration or a reduction in speed. The Planner should have noted that while the velocity remains positive as the parachutist continues to move downward, the acceleration becomes negative because the net force is upward due to the drag force from the chute. The error resembles a common problem in physics where directionality and sign convention are misapplied.
